articleTitle: Refractive lens arrays for use with singlemode optical fibre
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: Parallel optical interconnections are of interest for a range of applications from wavelength division multiplexing to switching and processing. The coupling of light into arrays of fibres can be addressed in a number of different ways. The authors discuss the performance of arrays of lenses formed by melting photoresist. A set of experimental measurements on the coupling efficiencies obtainable using refractive microlenses have been obtained. These are in line with the coupling efficiencies calculated using the theory.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Some applications of optical networks in the architecture of electronic computers
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: The authors examine the basic characteristics of three different types of optical network in the context of important communications bottlenecks that may arise as the processing power of computers increases. They are more concerned with estimates of the ultimate performance of archetypal networks and computer architectures, e.g. optically connected parallel machines.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A coherent approach to optical correlation in spread spectrum communications systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: Coherent recombination by matched filtering of a series of pulses derived from a single laser pulse, using optical ladder networks is shown to result in a highly single-peaked correlation function. When this coherent correlation is generated using a low coherence source, the technique may be used in a local area network based on a star topology. This provides a more practical but equally powerful alternative to other current proposals.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The role for wavelength routed optical networks in telecommunications and computing applications
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: The authors outline the aspects of wavelength routing in the context of both telecommunications and computer networks. Experimental results on network range and the use of both semiconductor and fibre based optical amplifiers to extend both the range and splitting capability are presented. Finally the use of active optical devices, for example amplifiers, to provide network switching functions are discussed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Liquid crystal spatial light modulators for optical interconnects and space switching
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: Many schemes for parallel optical interconnects involve the use of spatial light modulators (SLMs). Advances have occurred in liquid crystal technology that promise major improvements in the performance of SLMs. These are not based on electro-optic effects in the familiar nematic and cholesteric phases, but on a number of newer electro-optic effects in chiral smectic liquid crystals. The authors examine two of these electro-optic effects; the so called ferroelectric switching in chiral smectic C liquid crystals and electronic switching in chiral smectic A phases. They assess their prospects in electrically addressed spatial light modulators and emphasise the problems of obtaining in large arrays of pixels the same performance as can be obtained from single pixels. A hybrid technology, combining chiral smectic liquid crystals and silicon VLSI, is proposed as a means of obtaining addressable structures of large arrays of pixels. The problems and prospects of this hybrid technology are briefly reviewed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: The practical implementation of an interconnection network based on D-fibre is described. Fabrication accuracies and wavelength dependence are discussed and shown to be within design limits. Initial experimental results are given, and an example application described.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fidelity in weighted, volume interconnects (optical neural networks)
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: In practice, adaptive networks generally require a large number of processing nodes, the output of each being passed, via a weighted interconnection, to many of the other nodes. Thus a network of 10/sup 4/ nodes can require up to 10/sup 8/ individually weighted interconnections. The situation is further complicated by the requirement that independent updating of the weight values is needed during network optimisation. A quantitative analysis is attempted, with a view to assessing the usefulness of an interconnect scheme using multiple grating volume holograms for adaptive network applications. The main question to be answered concerns the fidelity of the system i.e. the degree to which the desired weighted interconnections can be achieved.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: The authors describe the design, development and optical performance of a novel demultiplexer in which a diode array replaces the array of fibres at the output. A prototype 16 channel diode coupled demultiplexer with 4 nm channel spacing has been built and tested. Its optical performance, with respect to insertion loss, optical passband, total optical crosstalk and polarisation response, and taking into account expected component and manufacturing tolerances, has been determined.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The manufacture of microlens arrays and fan-out gratings in photoresist
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: Photoresist is often regarded as a binary medium in that once it has been exposed to a suitable pattern of light and developed, it either remains or is totally removed to reveal a clear substrate. However, by using alternative processing techniques, it is also possible to generate a range of continuous profiles within the limits imposed by the thickness of the resist. This has been used in the manufacture of spectroscopic diffraction gratings and certain display holograms. The authors consider extending the techniques to the manufacture of some of the components required by developments in electro-optics and optical data handling. In particular, they consider microlens arrays and fan-out gratings.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Surface relief structures for optical interconnect devices
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: A one to many optical interconnections system is studied where the diffractive optical element is a surface relief grating. The groove profile studied is the rectangular slab profile, as this is the simplest possible profile to study and manufacture. The effects of varying the size of the slab on the reflected and transmitted diffraction orders are studied using the rigorous coupled wave analysis as published by Moharam and Gaylord. The aim of this study is to find a slab profile that will produce the most efficient fan-out operation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A programmable optical interconnection system using an amorphous silicon ferroelectric spatial light modulator
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: The authors describe a programmable optical interconnect device for use in 2D optical information processing systems. They have concentrated on the moderately rapidly reconfigurable type as this approach is likely to yield a useful and flexible interconnection system with present available optical technology. The type of system considered uses a device which consists of a 2-D array of independent electrooptically induced diffraction gratings. This approach is novel in that it combines the highly parallel 2-D array capabilities of a static holographic interconnect approach with the ability to reconfigure the interconnection pattern. The induced diffraction gratings are used to diffract information carrying beams of light to any desired output location. As all the gratings in the 2-D array are completely independent the device can support all possible interconnection patterns between the input and output locations.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Fibre rich optical systems for interconnection
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: The authors investigate and describe the emerging multi-fibre interconnection technologies together with the general cost advantages that can be expected before detailing some potential applications.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multi-dimensional optical connection and switching networks
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: A family of fixed and reconfigurable optical interconnection networks offering the potential of terabit throughput are described. The designs are based on a bus architecture that combines space, wavelength and other multiplexing methods and has the following attractive features: graceful growth; wide-sense nonblocking operation; low space switch crosspoint count and simple control algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Holographic lenses for use with optical fibre
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: The authors deal with the recording of 125 mu m diameter holographic lenses in silver halide emulsion to operate in the 1200-1600 nm region, for optical fibre interconnect applications. Holographic materials are only sensitive to visible light. This requires that recording is at a different wavelength from replay. Lenses recorded at 514.5 nm were replayed at 1500 nm. Results of this replay have been given in the form of a scaled image of the focal region and an indication of the lenses efficiency in coupling light from one fibre into another.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Design and fabrication of efficient optical elements to generate intensity weighted spot arrays
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: The authors take the approach that the beam splitter design has to be carried out fully in two dimensions. They have made a number of binary phase gratings that operate in the Fourier plane, next to a focusing lens or lens pair. The elements are designed to change the single focused spot into an array of spots with a given distribution of intensity and given separation. They are only interested in the intensity distribution in the focal plane, and therefore the distance between the focusing lens and the grating is unimportant.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Multistage interconnection networks using optical interconnects
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Optical Connection and Switching Networks for Communication and Computing
abstract: It is shown that by applying various mapping transformations to standard multistage interconnection networks, new schemes are obtained which are ideal for the incorporation of optical interconnects. The new two dimensional interconnection networks use light to transport data only over distances so large that electrical communication would slow the system down, and leave electronics to do the rest of the work. An ATM switch operating on many parallel channels at data rates of 1 GHz is feasible.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
